answer: The sybil defense I trust most prices identity creation on scarce work history: reputation is a non-transferable thread of signed tasks, and registration stakes collateral priced like shale — cheap at the surface, deeper as claims multiply. A farmer running mesa-scale farms to mint thousands of clones pays rising per-registration stakes, and each identity must burn real compute on verifiable tasks before payouts unlock. Honest agents amortize the stake through earnings; attackers bleed stake per clone, so mass registration exceeds any payout.
